subject: nineTailedKitsune
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: nine-tailed kitsune fox with spirit flames.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I need to plan this carefully as a single full module. I'm designing a kitsune fox standing on a small stone shrine dais with a rune ring, white/cream fur with red markings, nine tails fanned out with blue spirit flames at the tips, and floating foxfire orbs surrounding it.

I'm sketching out the skeleton structure next: hip root joint, a spine chain built from catmull points toward the chest, a neck and head chain, and legs with limb IK, plus nine separate tail chains, defining the color palette (white, cream, red, gold, ink, and two flame-blue tones) and working out joint placement coordinates.

I'm then sweeping the spine chain into a tapered body tube with varying radii, and adding a separate thinner sweep for the neck.

For coloring, I'm considering a countershaded coat paint (white belly, cream back) and thinking about adding red wavy stripe markings along the back.

Then I'm moving to the legs: four limbs using the limb helper, with front legs running from shoulder to foot with segmented lengths.

For the paws I'll add a gradient coloring from lighter coat to dark sock tones along each leg. Then for hind legs I'm setting up a three-segment digitigrade chain from hip to foot with appropriate lengths and bend directions for knee and hock joints.

Working out the limb point-and-span naming convention — confirming that for a chain with N segments I need N+1 points, and the last named point corresponds to the tip (paw). Front legs get three points for two spans, hind legs four points for three spans, with the foot sphere sitting low and slightly sunk for ground contact, then building the paw as a small flattened ellipsoid at the limb's end.

Shifting to the head, I'm placing it at the end of the neck and defining a local coordinate frame (forward/up) relative to the head joint so I can position features like the skull sphere and a snout shape -- trying a cone or sweep oriented along the forward direction, aimed slightly downward to form the muzzle.

I'm working out the cone orientation, placing the snout and nose, then adding a separate lower jaw joint with its own rod shape angled forward below the upper jaw.

Positioning ears as tall cones, I'm working out the geometry using a manual helper function that offsets from the head's base position rather than relying on the local-space naming conventions, to avoid ambiguity with left/right directions.

I'm simplifying the ear gradient to just vary by y-position, then moving on to the eyes -- planning to use decals placed on the skull surface with a fox-like slitted amber eye texture, mirrored for left/right sides.

For the markings, I'm adding red kitsune cheek streaks and a forehead diamond mark via decals, then building fluffy cheek ruffs out of small cones pointing outward, and starting on a neck ruff made of cones as well.

For the nine tails, I'm planning a fan arrangement radiating from the rump point, with each tail's angle and elevation varying across the fan so they spread out and curve upward and back symmetrically.

Making the center tail tallest with tapering radii for a fluffy fox-tail shape, and planning color bands transitioning from white to a fiery red tip, with named joints for each tail chain.

For the spirit flame effect at each tail tip, I'm using small glowing cone clusters colored flame-orange with an inner white glow layer, positioned above the tip points.

Adding flame card sprites...

For the nine tails I'm planning fur mottle patterns with cream and red gradient tips along each path, keeping the flame counts manageable. I'm also thinking about adding small glowing foxfire orbs floating fixed around the fox's hips for extra atmosphere.

Now I'm designing the stone dais base as a stepped hexagonal cylinder, and realizing I need to offset all fox joint coordinates upward by a constant so the base sits flush at ground level -- I'll wrap positions in a helper function that adds this Y offset automatically.

Still writing base geometry...

I'm adding stone lanterns at the dais corners—post, glowing lamp box, and cone roof—and considering whether a small torii gate would fit the composition.

I'll skip the ofuda charms but scatter a few flat sakura petal cards on the dais for detail. Now I'm building a red shimenawa-style rope necklace around the fox's neck with a gold bell sphere mounted at the front.

Positioning the bell sweep loop...

Using 0.11 for the collar. For the bell, I want it to hang under the throat, which means picking the ring item roughly 180° opposite the top — with 12 evenly spaced items, that's index 6. I'll place a small gold sphere there, offset slightly downward, attached to the second neck joint.

The ring's items array can double as points for a catmull curve, so the band geometry should work. I'll also add a gold crescent moon or forehead gem via decal, and design an eye texture with an almond amber iris, red outline, slit pupil, white highlight, and black lash details. I'll skip teeth and tongue, keep the mouth simple, and add red stripe markings along the body/back rather than on the legs, skipping leg bands and bracelets for now.

Still planning whisker placement, decal targeting onto the skull surface, cheek ruff cone positions, head-top hair tufts between the ears, and tail coloring with red spiral/ring patterns using a procedural paint function based on position along the tail.

Setting the center tail to gold, and defining each tail's paint inline since the sheet can share them. Now I'm working out the tail positions relative to the hips joint, tracing the spine chain's path upward from the base through several points.

Setting body sweep radii across spans to taper the torso shape, then defining the neck chain parented to the last spine joint so it continues smoothly from the chest point upward.

Adding head joint and leg root placements...

For the legs, I'm setting different sweep radii for front and hind limbs since the hind thigh should appear bulkier, and planning a dark gradient sock color for the lower legs. I'm also working out the hind leg's joint chain lengths and foot target position to keep the total reach consistent with the hip root.

Now I'm sketching helper functions: P and V to offset points and vectors by the ground height Y0, a cone helper for simple flat-shaded cone geometry, and a fluff helper that places small cone tufts of fur oriented along a direction vector, computing their center position from the bone position plus half their length.

I'm assigning head parts to the head bone and jaw parts to the jaw bone, then listing out the textures I'll need (eyes, cheek/forehead markings, runes, blue and violet flame glows), before sketching an SVG flame shape with layered gradient paths for the outer and inner flame silhouette.

Now I'm designing the runes SVG with concentric circles, radial glyph marks, and a nine-point star pattern to evoke a mystical ring, working out stroke widths so they scale properly at the target raster resolution.

Then I'm building a lantern helper that constructs a stone base, post, and glowing warm-colored lamp box nested inside a stone frame, with slab plates top and bottom and a simple roof cone.

I'm designing a mottled stone paint function that blends two gray-blue tones with noise and adds patches of moss color on upward-facing surfaces based on normal angle and additional noise thresholds.

Now I'm laying out the base lathe geometry for the dais with tiered radii, then considering a glowing cyan ring sweep around the top tier using a closed catmull or arc curve for the accent lighting.

For the orbs, I'm spacing around 6 of them in front-facing angles with varied radius and height, each a small glowing sphere topped with a flickering flame card, attached to the hips bone for frame alignment.

Now I'm sketching the eye SVG itself: an almond-shaped iris path with a fiery fill and dark outline, a curved red brow line above, a vertical slit pupil ellipse, and a small white highlight circle for shine.

Then I'm roughing out the facial decal marks: a cheek design made of three curved red swoosh strokes, and a forehead mark shaped like a diamond/crescent with a red outline and a gold inner circle, sizing everything proportionally for the raster output.

Now I'm positioning the decals relative to the skull geometry, defining the head's local coordinate frame off the HEAD base joint and placing the skull sphere using scaled dimensions anchored to that frame.

I'm working out eye placement relative to the skull's curved front surface, calculating projection directions so decals wrap correctly onto the sphere. I also need to check how the snout cone overlaps with eye positioning to make sure they don't visually clash.

Now I'm figuring out the cone geometry for the snout, orienting it with a forward-downward tilt, and positioning a small dark sphere for the nose tip at the front.

Then I'm sketching the jaw: setting a joint point and aim target, and building the lower jaw as a hexagonal rod spanning from the chin area forward, sized to sit comfortably below the snout's base radius so the proportions look right.

I'll skip the tongue for now, add tiny fang cones angled downward near the mouth tip, and finish with whiskers as thin spike elements radiating outward and slightly forward from the cheek area.

For the ears, I'm positioning cones angled outward on the skull with inner ear fluff shifted forward using a darker gradient color, and giving the ear tips a subtle gradient from white to dark plum for a shadowed effect.

Now I'm adding a small hair tuft on the crown using three cones angled back and up, and settling the overall head-to-body proportions to keep the cute look. For the cheeks, I'm layering several fluff tufts at different positions and angles to build up a fuller ruff effect around the face.

I'm also sketching in a red-gold sash that wraps around the body near the mid-spine joint, working out the right ring radius to sit just outside the body's elliptical cross-section there.

Then I'm thinking about a small gold ornament, maybe a flattened sphere, placed at the top of the ring, and considering adding painted red stripe markings across the back wherever the surface normal points upward and stays near the body's centerline.

For the stripe logic I'm making the top region switch to a distinct back-stripe pattern (narrow red bands with slight wobble, like tiger stripes) while the belly uses the countershaded cream, with a somewhat stylized hard edge between the two zones, plus some kumadori-style accent lines. Then I'm shifting focus to the legs, giving them a gradient fading from white to dark with a reddish tint on the upper portion.

Now I'm working out the tail fan geometry, computing nine tail positions spread across an angle range, with each tail curving upward and outward from a base point near the hindquarters, adjusting height and spread based on how far each tail sits from center so the middle tails rise higher and the side tails splay out more, while keeping the lantern orbs at the tips sized to avoid overlapping the hind legs or each other.

Still refining tail shapes and colors...

Still defining tail and ruff geometry...

Setting up the hips joint as root, then building the spine chain with a catmull-rom curve through four control points. For the legs, I'm looping over left and right sides, generating limb points with a bend direction vector, keeping consistent naming conventions for each side.

Still writing limb chains...

Defining the hind leg joint chain...

Still defining skull geometry... I also need to mirror eye decals for the opposite side, set the lantern roof rotation, and handle glow effects for rune textures with transparent circle geometry. I'm also checking which helper imports I'll need like gradient, countershade, stripes, paint, and mix.

I'm sketching out the stone base lathe profile with faceted segments, deciding against adding petals or paper streamers for now, and sizing the flame card geometry near the orb frame. I'm also setting the glow strength for tail tip flames before moving on to fur details.

Writing fluff helper function...
